It was a very disappointing experience.

I was interested in a particular cat and had visited the store several times to consider adopting it. At that time, I was told, "If anyone else is interested, we will contact you by phone, so please fill out the necessary paperwork." I provided my contact information and address. I was also making concrete preparations to welcome the cat into my home, with the intention of adopting it.

However, a few days later, I was surprised to see "A family has been found" displayed on the website. When I called to inquire, I was told the cat had already been sold.

When I mentioned, "I was told you would call if anyone was interested," the response was, "It seems we forgot," but for me, that was not an acceptable response.

Of course, I understand that since it's a cat, there's a possibility that someone else might end up buying it. I'm not complaining about not being able to purchase it.

However, because I was told they would contact me if anyone was interested, I had invested time and money in preparing to adopt that cat. Not only was the promise not fulfilled, but I was also unaware of the situation unless I proactively inquired, and when I contacted them by phone, there was no apology; the matter ended with a casual remark like, "It seems the person in charge forgot." This was extremely disappointing.

For those considering welcoming a cat into their family, this kind of communication and explanation is crucial.

Furthermore, if thorough operations are not possible, I would like them to stop the practice of unnecessarily requiring the submission of personal information in writing.

While I believe that meeting a cat is a matter of fate, I would have liked the store to handle this matter more honestly.

I visited again after a year for the same event. Just like last time, I mainly bought dog toys! They sell very colorful and cute items. I was spoiled for choice, but I ended up buying several things. I'll be back next year! I wonder if the event will continue?!


At the event held at Ariake GYM-EX:
I visited after having lunch at the food court. They sell very cute pet supplies. My dog ​​absolutely loves the bat toy I bought here!

The shop had a very strong smell.

I think it was the smell of an air freshener used to mask animal odors, but I couldn't stand it and left immediately.

Also, it seems the grooming salon is currently closed due to a staff shortage.

About 90% of the stock was dog supplies, dog food, and other pet products. There was hardly any cat food or cat supplies. Even the live animals for sale were mostly dogs. This store hardly has any cats. Perhaps it's because most of the local residents only have small dogs.

You'd be better off looking for cat food and cat supplies at other pet shops.

Akatsuka's attitude was disappointing. (I shouldn't even call him a doctor.)
I've used veterinary clinics many times, but I was disappointed with the way he treated me.
I don't know much about the technical aspects of treatment, but I think there's a lot of room for improvement in communication and how he treated his patients (pets). It was as if he was completely disrespectful of us. It was the first time I'd ever heard him speak so arrogantly.
Even before I even considered his medical skills, I felt he lacked basic interpersonal skills.
I'm disappointed that my experience left me with a sense of distrust after going to the clinic.
I strongly hope that he will thoroughly train his staff so that no more pet owners have to go through the same experience.

Thank you for your feedback on Pet Shop One Love Ariake Garden Tokyo Main Store. Your satisfaction is a great encouragement to all of our staff. We will strive to improve our services and create an environment where you can visit us with peace of mind. We look forward to your next visit.

The selection does not seem to be geared towards owners of multiple pets. Specifically, there are no 3.5kg or 4.0kg packages of food for either dogs or cats like those found at PETEMO, CAINZ, or Kojima.
Apart from that, there are also products that I have never seen anywhere else, so I use the store to purchase those items.
They sell live animals at reasonable prices that are the same as or slightly cheaper than other stores. I felt that they treated live animals more conscientiously than the shop in Viva Home in Toyosu.

The other day, I went to buy a present for my friend's puppy.
Since I've never owned a dog myself, I showed the shop assistant a picture of the puppy and asked, "I don't know its age, but can it eat this treat?" They told me that because the puppy looked so young, anything that wasn't suitable for a puppy under three months old might be problematic.
Later, I found out the puppy was exactly three months old! Amazing!
(After hearing this, I bought some baby biscuits just in case, so it was all good!)

By the way, if you search for "tropical fish," this shop comes up, but they don't sell tropical fish, aquatic plants, or aquariums. °･🐠

While shopping with my dog, I came across a store offering dog food samples. They explained the product to me and gave me a sample, which I'm looking forward to trying. There were also various toys that dogs would love, and since it was the change of seasons, they were having a sale on seasonal items, so I was spoiled for choice. I'd like to visit again.

The selection was decent. However, I felt there were few high-quality items. The impression was that the items were the kind you'd find at a hardware store or similar.

When I visited the store, there were no staff members inside, and they only came out after I rang the doorbell at the register. I felt a little uneasy.
I was able to successfully welcome into my home the adorable little one I saw at first sight!

It's always a lifesaver because it's so close by.

The manager and everyone else are incredibly friendly.

My dog ​​is always treated so kindly, and it's one of my favorite shops.

Sometimes the staff are in the back and not readily visible, but it's a very kind and welcoming shop.

I think they have a great selection of products.

As a regular customer, they're always flexible and accommodating, making it an indispensable spot for dog owners.

The toy poodle puppy was absolutely adorable. Its gait was so unique! It was so charming, I'm sure it'll find a new owner very soon. It's such a shame I can't adopt it.

Overall, there were many puppies and kittens around three months old, and just looking at them was so calming.

I currently have three cats, so I could only buy cat food, but I'd love to come back.

The only thing that bothered me was their emphasis on installment payments.

Is this normal for pet shops? I questioned why they were recommending installment payments at such a high price.

I went there hoping to buy a dog, but there wasn't a single one...lol
The two staff members who were there were talking to each other, so I couldn't ask why there weren't any.
The store smelled bad; I wondered if it was poorly managed or something.
I started to feel uneasy, wondering if it's better not to get a dog here.
Quite expensive due to the location

I came here with my dog ​​because it looked nice on Google Images, but it was smaller than I expected.
Surprisingly small.

They also had some rare treats on sale, so I bought one.

I didn't feel like I needed to go out of my way to buy anything, so we only stayed for less than five minutes.
I was surprised to see three squirrels at this time of year. It's rare to see baby squirrels at this time of year. I highly recommend this place to anyone looking to adopt a squirrel.
And why not bring back something for your pet? Well, you'll find what you're looking for here.

Reservations for the following month open on the 5th of each month, but even if you keep calling from 10 AM onwards, it's uncertain whether you'll be able to get an appointment.

I used their services twice, but stopped going because the staff member's attitude and the dog's compatibility were terrible.

The second time, I thought the notification that they were finished came unusually quickly, and they said they couldn't cut the fur because the dog was resisting, so they returned the dog with a short body and a very bushy face. Of course, they charged me the full amount.

(My dog ​​has never resisted grooming at other salons, and he doesn't get angry or resist when I cut his fur at home.)
The second time I dropped him off, they said, "We'll do what we can today!" and when I went to pick him up, they made sarcastic remarks. There are many dog-owning households in the area, but this is the only grooming salon, so I think they treat their dog this way because losing one customer won't have much impact on them.

The shop staff are all very friendly, so I think I just happened to get a bad match, but the service was absolutely awful.

The pet shop was good.

The attached hospital was the worst I've ever experienced.

Their knowledge level was about the same as mine, or even lower.

They didn't tell me anything I needed to know beforehand, so I couldn't do anything that needed to be done today.

They got angry and said, "We only accept online reservations, so we have no way to tell you!"

Is that okay? Is that my responsibility? It was a terrible place overall.
